h: Make your West End game count
p: An escape room is a great way to bring a scattered group together in London. Mates coming in from different corners of the capital can meet at Tottenham Court Road, play a game and head straight off for food, with no faffing about. Tourists love it too, as a change of pace from queuing for landmarks.

Some pointers for a winning run. Before the clock starts, decide who's tracking time and who's keeping hold of found items. Search thoroughly before you try to solve, because half the battle is gathering every piece of the puzzle. Don't force anything that won't move, and if you've been going round in circles for a few minutes, ask for a hint. Nobody's handing out medals for stubbornness.

Location-wise, you're spoilt rotten. The Dominion Theatre sits right by Tottenham Court Road station, and the towering Centre Point is just above it. Soho Square is a leafy little escape a few minutes south, and if you head west along Oxford Street you'll reach the Liberty building and the colourful shops of Carnaby Street, just off Regent Street. To the north, Fitzrovia's Charlotte Street is packed with restaurants for a post-game feast. Covent Garden, with its street performers and market halls, is an easy walk south-east as well. The Elizabeth line at Tottenham Court Road makes it quick to get across London, right out to Heathrow or across to Canary Wharf, so even groups staying outside the centre can get there easily.
